chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Visit your dead, for they rejoice at your visitation, and let each of you seek his need at the grave of his father and at the grave of his mother, with whatever he supplicates for them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting the graves of parents in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith establishes the spiritual efficacy of grave visitation (Ziyarat) by highlighting the deceased's awareness and joy, a concept supported by Shia scholars who view it as a means of strengthening familial bonds and facilitating intercession. It specifically directs believers to present their needs and offer supplications at the graves of parents, emphasizing the unique status of maternal and paternal figures in Islamic piety.
